text: Working with APIs is a fundamental skill for modern developers. When you make an HTTP request to an API, you usually send a method like GET or POST, and the server responds with data in JSON format, which is easy to read and parse. Most APIs require authentication, often using an API key or a token, to ensure only authorized users access the service. However, you must also respect rate limits, which control how many requests you can make in a given time period; exceeding them may result in temporary blocks. Finally, robust error handling is essential. Always check the status code in the response and write code to manage errors gracefully, such as retrying or showing a friendly message.
